chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn Uqba and Ghalib ibn Usman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When it is evening, say: 'O Allah! I ask You at the approaching of Your night and the departure of Your day, and the presence of Your prayers and the sounds of Your supplications, that You send prayers upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and supplicate with whatever you like.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended evening supplication in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication emphasizes the transitional moment of evening as a time of divine attentiveness, linking the believer's voice to the celestial 'prayers' (salawat) of Allah. It reflects the Shia tradition of combining specific invocations for the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt with personal, spontaneous du'a, highlighting the intimacy of the believer's relationship with the Divine during the shift from day to night.
